subject: English Language
title: Pronouns
introduction: Learn how pronouns work, then practise five questions at a time.

rules.title: Subject and object pronouns
rules.body: Use I, he, she, we and they as subjects. Use me, him, her, us and them after verbs and prepositions.
rules.example: My sister and I went. · The teacher spoke to her.

rules.title: Possessive words
rules.body: Mine, yours, his, hers, ours and theirs stand alone. My, your, her, our and their come before a noun. Whose asks or tells who owns something.
rules.example: This bag is hers. · Her bag is blue. · Whose bag is this?

rules.title: Reflexive and emphatic
rules.body: Myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves and themselves refer back to the subject. A reflexive pronoun is needed by the verb; an emphatic pronoun adds emphasis.
rules.example: She hurt herself. · She herself completed the work.

rules.title: Relative, interrogative and indefinite
rules.body: Who, whom, whose, which and that can link a clause to a noun. Who and which can ask questions. Someone and nobody refer to unspecified people.
rules.example: The boy who won smiled. · Who won? · Nobody answered.

worked.prompt: The coach asked he to join the team.
worked.answer: The coach asked him to join the team.
worked.explanation: Asked needs an object pronoun, so use him.

questions.prompt: 7. Which of the following sentences uses the emphatic pronoun correctly?

options.text: (c) She was hurt by the fall.
(d) The assignment was completed by her.

questions.explanation: An emphatic pronoun adds emphasis to the noun or pronoun it refers to.

questions.prompt: 8. Which of the following sentences has a possessive pronoun?

options.text: (a) Everyone should submit the book on Monday.
(b) Someone left a phone on the table.
(d) This is the pen I was looking for.

questions.explanation: Theirs stands alone and shows ownership.

questions.prompt: (a) My friend baked a cake that was delicious.
questions.explanation: that — relative identifies the pronoun and its kind.

questions.prompt: (b) Nobody could explain why the system failed during the test.
questions.explanation: Nobody — indefinite identifies the pronoun and its kind.

questions.prompt: (c) The coach praised himself for the team’s victory.
questions.explanation: himself — reflexive identifies the pronoun and its kind.

questions.prompt: (d) Which of these options do the girls prefer?
questions.explanation: Which — interrogative identifies the pronoun and its kind.

questions.prompt: (e) This cafe always plays the songs I like.
questions.explanation: I — personal identifies the pronoun and its kind.

questions.prompt: Maya and ___ will present the project.
questions.explanation: Subject pronoun: I fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: The librarian handed the books to Rohan and ___.
questions.explanation: Object pronoun: me fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: This notebook belongs to me; that one belongs to you. That one is ___.
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun: yours fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: The children packed their bags by ___.
questions.explanation: Reflexive pronoun: themselves fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: The head girl ___ welcomed the visitors.
questions.explanation: Emphatic pronoun: herself fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: The scientist ___ discovered the medicine won an award.
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun: who fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: ___ left this umbrella in the hall?

questions.prompt: ___ of the two answers is correct; both are wrong.

questions.prompt: Mira owns the red scarf. The red scarf is ___.
questions.explanation: Possessive pronoun: hers fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: The boys blamed ___, accepting responsibility for their own error.

questions.prompt: She ___ solved the difficult puzzle.
questions.explanation: Emphatic pronoun: herself fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: This is the house ___ we visited last summer.
questions.explanation: Relative pronoun: that fits this sentence.

questions.prompt: Those pencils belong to us; these belong to them. These are ___.

questions.prompt: The puppy hurt ___ while jumping.

questions.prompt: The principal called Anika and ___.

questions.prompt: One by one, ___ of the guests received a name card.

questions.prompt: The artist ___ paintings we admired spoke to us.
questions.explanation: Possessive relative pronoun: whose fits this sentence.
